summary.title: Introduction to Algorithms (SMA 5503) | MIT OpenCourseWare 6.046J
summary.one_liner: An MIT OpenCourseWare course covering techniques for designing and analyzing efficient algorithms, with an emphasis on methods useful in practice.
keywords: sma 5503 analysis and design of algorithms
takeaways: Covers core algorithm design paradigms such as divide-and-conquer and dynamic programming.
Covers data structures like search trees, heaps, and hashing, plus amortized analysis.
Includes graph algorithms, shortest paths, network flow, and computational geometry.
Also covers number-theoretic, polynomial and matrix algorithms, caching, and parallel computing.
The course was also taught under the Singapore-MIT Alliance as SMA 5503.
summary.summary: This is the MIT OpenCourseWare page for 6.046J Introduction to Algorithms, also offered as SMA 5503 (Analysis and Design of Algorithms) in the Singapore-MIT Alliance programme. The course description says it teaches techniques for designing and analyzing efficient algorithms, with emphasis on practical methods. It lists topics including sorting, search trees, heaps, hashing, divide-and-conquer, dynamic programming, amortized analysis, graph and shortest-path algorithms, network flow, computational geometry, number-theoretic, polynomial and matrix algorithms, caching, and parallel computing. The page text is a short course description with no lecture content. The listing notes that the course can be watched and downloaded on OCW and that newer courses exist.
